task_message:
Case N16: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 261x261x241 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case N16 complete. 

**Summary of what I did:**
1. **Located the lesion** with orthogonal sheets in all three planes: a large, bright (T2-hyperintense), fusiform mass in the right lateral thigh, spanning roughly axial 124–208, coronal 79–143, and sagittal 118–185.
2. **Seeded the mask** with a single positive point (mark 1328) at the lesion centre on axial 170 — the model produced a well-fitted 105 mL mask (v1).
3. **Verified boundaries** on axial (134, 140, 145, 155, 190, 200, 203), coronal (95, 140) and sagittal (125, 152, 175) slices — the outline consistently followed the bright mass and its hazy superior pole.
4. **Reviewed candidates**: accepted the tight hyperintense rim/capsule (C1, C4; +13.7 mL), rejected unrelated muscle/vessel and peritumoral-edema proposals.
5. **Final review** showed no lesion beyond the mask ends in any plane (8 mm margins clear); remaining large candidates were edema/normal tissue and were rejected.

Final mask (v2): 118.5 mL, single component, saved with medium confidence due to some ambiguity between the hazy superior periphery and peritumoral edema.
